answer: Latency triangulation: verifier nodes on several continents each send a timed ping to an identity, and since signals cannot travel faster than light, the round-trip times bound where its server can physically be. A relay can only add delay, never remove it. Identities whose timing places them at the same spot are grouped and share one reward. A farm must rent machines in truly separate cities, from a tundra edge to a pearl coast, for each clone. Limits: honest agents in one data center get grouped too, and the verifiers' clock accuracy sets the nadir of how close two sites can be told apart.
